pull_request.title: Expose fallible fixture admission on published Memory 0.40
pull_request.body:
Jobs needs fixture-cell setup refusals returned through its existing error boundary; Blob's published fixture constructor deliberately panics. Extend the published Memory 0.40 helper with `FixtureCell::try_new`, typed `FixtureCellError`, explicit committed-authority verification and `into_memory` for caller-owned corruption/retention inspection. The existing constructor shares the same admission path and retains its panic convention.

This replaces draft #111 with a narrow contribution on delivered 0.40.0. It includes none of that draft's inherited, unpublished bounded constructors. Share the existing envelope validator internally: the ledger reader retains its existing byte ceiling; the trusted fixture opener validates headers before Cell initialization can replace non-Cell memory. Callers keep codecs, initialization, decode/write budgets, lifecycle and Job::restore. Raw Memory operations/initial publication can still panic, and bootstrap may commit ledger metadata before later envelope refusal. No reset or old-format reader is introduced.

Focused Linux qualification on Rust 1.91: five feature tests and twelve stable-cell tests pass, including typed admission refusals, committed payload transfer and non-Cell header preservation. Strict feature Clippy, feature Wasm compilation, Rustdoc, formatting and links pass on the unchanged upstream lockfile. An isolated Jobs caller using both pending producer sources passes all 23 consumer tests, five capture tests, release Wasm, harness compilation, native/Wasm Clippy and separate floor checks. The frozen two-slot image remains refused without writes and frozen Jobs JSON still reopens. Qualification-only path overrides are not downstream publication/adoption.

Full repository CI, native macOS and live recovery were not run locally. Jobs keeps its published Memory dependency and tested adoption patch pending reviewed publication; https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-jobs/issues/50 owns that acceptance. No integration, release, publication or installation retirement is authorized by this PR.

issue.body:
Jobs needs fixture setup failures returned through its management/storage error boundary, while the existing Blob probe constructors deliberately panic. Extend #105 on its existing topic branch rather than duplicating the helper feature. Related: #104.

Add one typed fallible admission path, explicit committed-authority verification and transfer of the admitted virtual memory for corruption/retention inspection. Existing constructors share that admission path and retain their panic convention. Trusted unbounded opening validates existing Cell metadata before initialization; codecs, byte/work policy, lifecycle and Job::restore remain consumer-owned. No old ledger reader, reset, new backing memory fallback or package-version change is introduced. Raw Memory operations and initial Cell publication retain their substrate panic behavior.

Focused evidence:
- Seven Memory feature tests pass on Rust 1.88, including typed declaration/grant/bootstrap/configuration refusals and non-Cell header preservation.
- Strict feature Clippy, Rustdoc and Rust 1.88 Wasm compilation pass on the unchanged parent lockfile (Host 0.18.2).
- An isolated Jobs adoption using the candidate source passes all 23 consumer tests, five capture tests, release Wasm, harness compilation, native/Wasm Clippy and separate core/consumer floor checks. Its selected Host 0.18.4 graph is recorded separately. The original two-slot image remains refused without writes; Jobs JSON still reopens on current memory.

Draft pending the producer PR #105, its required qualification and review. Full Memory validation and live/native macOS qualification were not run locally. Jobs keeps published Memory 0.39.0; its tested adoption patch awaits a reviewed release. This PR authorizes no integration, publication or retained-installation reset.

issue.body:
## Delivered producer — Memory 0.45.0

The bounded/fallible FixtureCell extension from PR #105 and the superseded #116 is delivered in Memory 0.45.0. The current API provides typed setup/write refusal, explicit bounded fresh/retained entry points and admitted-memory transfer. Header, capacity and byte limits are admitted before payload loading; missing/corrupt retained cells are not initialized as fresh. Writes refuse oversize values before mutation. The fixture keeps its Cell/handle and ceiling after the temporary bootstrap runtime is dropped. The redundant authority recheck from the earlier PR is removed under the current successful-bootstrap contract.

Codecs, initialization, retained-data disposition and lifecycle remain consumer-owned. Bootstrap may update ledger metadata before a later Cell refusal; substrate IO/publication may panic. Jobs #50 and the linked Blob/Auth adoption remain separate consumer work. Their older-source evidence does not establish current adoption.

## Accepted delivery

Released Memory **0.45.0**, `93463259a07295f50146beb57c36adab303d9a37`, retains this implementation and its owning regression checks. The [complete current CI matrix](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-memory/actions/runs/38931395729) passes tooling lint and all three full-test, MSRV and installed-runtime lanes (Ubuntu, macOS ARM and macOS Intel). The full-test gate includes release-helper/adapters and explicit fixture-cell feature qualification; MSRV checks all targets with `test-support`. The selected snapshot is Shared Tooling 0.15.0, `3bef3f2daec7f64f875397ed4d53d5b9e2e68a08`. Earlier failed/cancelled runs remain historical evidence. This completes this issue’s producer/adoption acceptance; it does not claim downstream application adoption.

issue.title: Add bounded fallible fixture-cell admission on Memory 0.44

repository.name: ic-memory
repository.description: Durable stable-memory allocation governance for Internet Computer canisters

issue.body:
Reconcile bounded fixture admission from this PR and typed setup/memory transfer from #116 against released Memory 0.44.0. Refs #104; supersedes #116 once this refreshed contribution is available for review.

`test-support` adds typed setup/write refusal, explicit bounded fresh/retained entry points and admitted-memory transfer. Retained headers, capacity and selected byte limits are checked before Cell loads its payload; invalid retained bytes are never initialized as fresh. Existing `new`/`set` keep their panic convention. The temporary runtime is dropped after authority verification and opening, retaining only the cell/handle and its ceiling. Codecs, initialization and lifecycle remain caller-owned. Bootstrap can advance allocation-ledger metadata before later Cell refusal; backing IO and publication can still panic.

The one header-admission helper serves both fixtures and the unchanged bounded ledger reader. There is no dependency or stored-format change. Pending notes select compatible 0.44.1 without changing package versions or lockfiles.

Validation on the reconciled source: 197 library tests pass (six explicit allocation measurements remain ignored); all eight fixture tests pass, including retained-header preservation, header-only oversized refusal, bounded writes, short replacement and missing Cell admission. Strict feature Clippy, warning-denied feature Rustdoc, formatting, Rust 1.91 native/all-target and Wasm checks, and current-toolchain feature Wasm compilation pass. All five default-feature raw Wasm probes have no size increase: core −97 bytes, diagnostics unchanged in size, admission −105, runtime integration −91 and installed IO −91.

Full release validation, installed qualification of this new head and native macOS acceptance were not run locally. Required hosted checks remain separate. Blob, Jobs and Auth adoption still requires this extension to be integrated/published and qualified by those consumers; their earlier-source evidence is not current adoption.

+## Fallible fixture admission

@@ -1,5 +1,16 @@
 # 0.40 release notes
 
+## [0.40.1]
+
+`testing::FixtureCell::try_new` returns `FixtureCellError` with typed runtime
+sources and verifies committed authority before opening. Existing non-Cell or
+malformed headers refuse before Cell initialization; admission never substitutes
+new backing memory. `new` shares this path with its existing panic convention.
+`into_memory` transfers the admitted grant for consumer corruption/retention tests.
+Callers retain codecs, initialization and byte/work policy. This trusted fixture
+opener adds no payload ceiling; substrate operations can still panic and bootstrap
+can commit ledger metadata before a later envelope refusal.
